A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TQA survey. Their complete text, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison, including matching the reordered appendix sections and renamed references.

before.justification: Appendix A.1 and Figure 4 report original descriptive analysis of the authors' 215-paper collection, including annual counts and thematic proportions. The model performance results in Figure 5 are separately attributed to prior studies.

after.justification: Appendix A.2 reports a 277-paper collection, and Figure 4 provides revised annual counts and thematic proportions. These constitute original descriptive data analysis; Figure 5 still reproduces results from cited studies.

M1.justification: Neither version proposes its own TQA algorithm or model. Added descriptions of reward models, RAPO, and graph/tree approaches review methods attributed to other work.

E1.justification: Table 2 adds eight catalogued datasets, including TABLET and SPARTA, but these are surveyed resources rather than datasets newly used by the authors for training or evaluation. The survey retains its TQA, table fact verification, and relevant Text-to-SQL scope.

E2.justification: Figure 5 retains the same Gemini, GPT-4, fine-tuned model, and OCR comparisons. Adding Xu et al. (2026a) to Table 1 changes research positioning, not the membership of an evaluated TQA baseline comparison.

E3.justification: For the descriptive literature analysis, the inclusion cutoff moves from August 1, 2025 to April 1, 2026, and the corpus grows from 215 to 277 papers. This changes the analysis sample while retaining the search sources, keywords, and selection approach; no new model-evaluation protocol is reported.

E4.justification: Neither version reports original TQA ablations, robustness experiments, or error analyses. Additional references to attention analysis and internal mechanisms expand the literature discussion without introducing an analysis conducted by this work.

E5.justification: Both versions report descriptive corpus counts and proportions without repeated-run information, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Changed counts do not alter the statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: Figure 4 changes the 2023/2024/2025 paper counts from 43/62/78 to 44/63/101, and the reported corpus total increases from 215 to 277. Table 2 adds entries and revises statistics, including 3.5k questions for TabularGSM versus 6.7k for the matched TabularMath entry. Figure 5's performance values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Neither version contains formal theorems, proofs, or mathematical derivations. New descriptions of graph structures and reward optimization are prose summaries of cited methods.

C1.justification: The introduction removes the explicit claim to be the first survey dedicated to TQA in the LLM era. The abstract and conclusion retain the central contributions: task taxonomy, challenge-based method review, evaluation coverage, and future directions.

C2.justification: Section 5 extends existing themes with learned modality selection, right-to-left and lexical challenges in multilingual TQA, mechanistic interpretability, and ambiguous real-world queries. These add substantive explanations and applicability considerations within the retained discussion framework; the principal stated limitations remain.

D1.justification: The paper-collection documentation updates its cutoff, and Table 2 supplies source, size, representation, and modality information for new resource entries. Existing descriptions also change: WikiMixQA is now documented as supporting single/multiple HTML tables with text and image context. These are catalog revisions, not evidence of rerun experiments.

R1.justification: The review substantially expands its coverage of reward-model ranking, test-time reasoning, visual table learning, graph/tree representations, and mechanistic interpretability. Table 1 adds Xu et al. (2026a), and Table 2 adds eight dataset references. These substantive additions extend beyond the numerous bibliographic and publication-version updates.

P1.justification: The introduction and task-setup descriptions undergo substantial rewriting, Section 3.2 reorganizes existing material around tools, prompting, and verification, and several Section 5 discussions are reworked. Appendix A.1 and A.2 exchange positions. The editing is extensive despite retaining the main section hierarchy.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn with numbered categories and a revised caption; Figures 2 and 3 move earlier and receive label refinements. Figure 4 extends its vertical scale, Table 1 gains a row, and Table 2 gains and redistributes rows. The basic plot designs and table columns remain.

improvement.justification: V2 provides a more useful synthesis by distinguishing policy training from reward-model ranking and adding concrete multilingual and interpretability considerations. The clarified Figure 1 and updated resource catalog also help readers. These gains are tempered by a new inconsistency: Section 1 describes Xu et al. (2026a) as text-only, whereas Table 1 lists text and image coverage.
